badr_lifetime_limit_cut.description: Candidate measure. From 6 April 2027 the lifetime limit on gains qualifying for Business Asset Disposal Relief falls from £1 million to £500,000; the relief rate stays at 18%. Gains above the limit pay the main capital gains tax rates. The model applies the limit to each year's gains. Capital gains are imputed and calibrated to 2024-25, when disposals were unusually high ahead of the April 2025 rise in the relief's rate, so the relief's base, and the revenue from restricting it, are likely 1.5 to 1.7 times too high.
badr_lifetime_limit_cut.name: Business Asset Disposal Relief restricted
badr_lifetime_limit_cut.reason: Taken out of the candidate set by decision (27 October 2026); not a measure the page shows.

domestic_electricity_zero_vat.description: Candidate measure. VAT on domestic electricity is 0% instead of 5% from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2028: the zero rate to March 2027, not in the model's baseline, scored with a candidate one-year extension. Applied to electricity spending only, in Great Britain (Northern Ireland keeps the 5%). 2026-27 carries the October to March share of a year's electricity use (about 57%), not a share of its days.
domestic_electricity_zero_vat.name: Zero VAT on domestic electricity

fuel_duty_rise_deferral.description: Candidate measure. Fuel duty stays at 52.95p a litre through winter 2026-27, with no April 2027 RPI rise; the 5p is restored in 2027-28 (3p on 1 September, 2p on 1 December 2027), and RPI uprating resumes in April 2028 from 57.95p, so that rise is never made up. Rates are day-weighted to fiscal years. Includes the VAT on the lower pump price.
fuel_duty_rise_deferral.name: Fuel duty rises deferred

road_fuel_vat_cut.description: Candidate measure. VAT on petrol and diesel falls from 20% to 15% from 1 December 2026 to 31 May 2027, fully passed through to pump prices; spending on fuel is held fixed. Day-weighted to fiscal years.
road_fuel_vat_cut.name: VAT cut on road fuel

state_pension_income_tax_protection.description: Candidate measure. From 6 April 2027, people over State Pension age get an income tax allowance equal to the full new State Pension (rounded up to £10: £13,040 in 2027-28), withdrawn £1 for £1 of income above it, down to the standard personal allowance. Someone whose only income is the full new State Pension pays no income tax.
state_pension_income_tax_protection.name: State Pension income tax protection

threshold_freeze_2031_32.description: Candidate measure. The income tax personal allowance stays at £12,570 and the basic rate band at £37,700 (a higher rate threshold of £50,270) for one more year, 2031-32, instead of rising with inflation to £12,830 and £38,500. From 2031-32 policyengine-uk sets the National Insurance primary threshold and upper earnings limit at the personal allowance and higher rate threshold, so they stay at £12,570 and £50,270 too; the employer secondary threshold is not held.
threshold_freeze_2031_32.name: Threshold freeze to 2031-32

warm_home_discount_top_up.description: Candidate measure. The Warm Home Discount rises from £150 to £250 for winter 2026-27 only: £100 more to each household in Great Britain receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit or income-related ESA. Receipt follows DESNZ's rates: 85% of Pension Credit households and 70% of other eligible households. Eligibility follows England and Wales's 2026-27 core group, so households in Scotland are approximate.
warm_home_discount_top_up.name: Warm Home Discount top-up
